- **[[C.01.014.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A manufacturer of a drug may make an
  application for a drug identification number for that drug.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (1) shall be made to
  the Minister in writing and shall include the following information
  and material:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the manufacturer of the drug as it will
    appear on the label;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pharmaceutical form in which the drug is to be
    sold;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any drug other than a drug described
    in paragraph (d), the recommended route of administration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug for disinfection in premises,
    the types of premises for which its use is recommended;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a quantitative list of the medicinal ingredients
    contained in the drug by their proper names or, if they have no
    proper names, by their common names;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the brand name under which the drug is to be sold;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} an indication of whether the drug is for human use
    or veterinary use;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name and quantity of each colouring ingredient
    that is not a medicinal ingredient;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the use or purpose for which the drug is
    recommended;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the recommended dosage of the drug;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the address of the manufacturer referred to in
    paragraph (a) and, where the address is outside the country, the
    name and address of the importer of the drug;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of any individual, firm,
    partnership or corporation, other than the names and addresses
    referred to in paragraphs (a) and (k), that will appear on the label
    of the drug;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug for veterinary use, the
    written text of every label to be used in connection with the drug,
    including any package insert and any document that is provided on
    request and that sets out supplementary information on the use of
    the drug;

  - [(m.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug for human use, mock-ups of
    every label to be used in connection with the drug --- including any
    package insert and any document that is provided on request and that
    sets out supplementary information on the use of the drug --- and
    mock-ups of the drug's packages;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the name and title of the person who signed the
    application and the date of signature; and

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug for human use, an assessment
    as to whether there is a likelihood that the drug will be mistaken
    for another drug for which a drug identification number has been
    assigned due to a resemblance between the brand name that is
    proposed to be used in respect of the drug and the brand name,
    common name or proper name of the other drug.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a new drug, a new drug submission, an
  extraordinary use new drug submission, an abbreviated new drug
  submission or an abbreviated extraordinary use new drug submission
  filed under section C.08.002, C.08.002.01 or C.08.002.1 shall be
  regarded as an application for a drug identification number.

- **[[C.01.014.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), if a
  manufacturer has provided all the information and material described
  in subsection C.01.014.1(2) or section C.08.002, C.08.002.01 or
  C.08.002.1, as the case may be, in respect of a drug, the Minister
  shall issue to the manufacturer a document that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sets out

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the drug identification number assigned for the
      drug, preceded by the abbreviation "DIN", or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if there are two or more brand names for the
      drug, the drug identification numbers assigned by the Minister for
      the drug, each of which pertains to one of the brand names and is
      preceded by the abbreviation "DIN"; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contains the information referred to in paragraphs
    C.01.014.1(2)(a) to (f).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may refuse to issue the document
  referred to in subsection (1) if he or she has reasonable grounds to
  believe that the product in respect of which an application referred
  to in section C.01.014.1 has been made

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is not a drug, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a drug but its sale would cause injury to the
    health of the purchaser or consumer or would be a contravention of
    the Act or these Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister refuses to issue the document under
  subsection (2), the manufacturer may submit additional information or
  material and request the Minister to reconsider his or her decision.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} On the basis of the additional information or
  material submitted under subsection (3), the Minister shall reconsider
  the grounds on which the refusal to issue the document was made.

**[[C.01.014.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.4 .sectionLabel}** If the
information referred to in subsection C.01.014.1(2) in respect of a drug
is no longer correct owing to a change in the subject matter of the
information,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a change in the subject matter of any
  of the information referred to in paragraphs C.01.014.1(2)(a) to (f)

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} that occurs prior to the sale of the drug, a new
    application shall be made, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} that occurs after the sale of the drug, no further
    sale of the drug shall be made until a new application for a drug
    identification number in respect of that drug is made and a number
    is assigned; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a change in the subject matter of any
  of the information referred to in paragraphs C.01.014.1(2)(g) to (k)

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} that occurs prior to the sale of the drug, the
    particulars of the change shall be submitted with the return of the
    document referred to in section C.01.014.3, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} that occurs after the sale of the drug, the person
    to whom the drug identification number in respect of that drug was
    issued shall, within 30 days of the change, inform the Minister of
    the change.

  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer to whom a document

- **[[C.01.014.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall cancel the
  assignment of a drug identification number for a drug if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer to whom a document was issued
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification
    number advises under section C.01.014.7 that they discontinued the
    sale of the drug; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Minister determines that the product for which
    the drug identification number has been assigned is not a drug.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may cancel the assignment of a drug
  identification number for a drug if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer to whom a document was issued
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification
    number contravenes section C.01.014.5;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer to whom a document was issued
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification
    number has been notified under section C.01.013 that the evidence
    that they submitted with respect to the drug is not sufficient; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the drug is a new drug in respect of which the
    notice of compliance has been suspended under section C.08.006.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may cancel the assignment of a drug
  identification number for a drug if, after he or she has, under
  section 21.31 of the Act, ordered the holder of a therapeutic product
  authorization referred to in subparagraph C.01.052(1)(a)(i) or (iii)
  to conduct an assessment of the drug in order to provide evidence
  establishing that the benefits associated with the drug outweigh the
  risks of injury to health,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder fails to comply with the order; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder complies with the order but the Minister
    determines that the results of the assessment are not sufficient to
    establish that the benefits associated with the drug outweigh the
    risks of injury to health.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, the Minister's power to cancel
  the assignment of a drug identification number

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under paragraph (2)(b) is not affected by his or
    her power to cancel the assignment of such a number under subsection
    (3); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under subsection (3) is not affected by his or her
    power to cancel the assignment of such a number under paragraph
    (2)(b).

#### [Shortages of Drugs and Interruption and Discontinuation of Sale of Drugs]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575006 .Subheading}

**[[C.01.014.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.7 .sectionLabel}** The
manufacturer to whom a document was issued under subsection
C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification number assigned for
a drug shall, within 30 days after the day on which they discontinue the
sale of the drug, submit the following information to the Minister:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the drug identification number assigned for the drug;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the manufacturer discontinued the
  sale of the drug; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the latest expiration date of the drug that the
  manufacturer sold and the lot number of that drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/81-248, s. 2
- SOR/2016-139, s. 5
- SOR/2017-259, s. 8
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.014.7-20170314.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.014.7"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.014.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.71 .sectionLabel}** If a
period of 12 months has elapsed since the day on which the manufacturer
to whom a document was issued under subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets
out the drug identification number assigned for a
[[drug]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section C.01.014.8 last
sold the drug, the manufacturer shall so notify the Minister in writing
within 30 days after the day on which that period ends.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-259, s. 8
:::

**[[C.01.014.72]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.72 .sectionLabel}** If the
manufacturer to whom a document was issued under subsection
C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification number assigned for
a drug resumes the sale of the drug after a period of 12 months has
elapsed since the day on which they last sold the drug, the manufacturer
shall so notify the Minister in writing within 30 days after the day on
which they resume the sale of the drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-259, s. 8
:::

**[[C.01.014.8]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.8 .sectionLabel}** The
following definitions apply in this section and in sections C.01.014.9
to C.01.014.14.

[[drug]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[drug]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any of the following drugs for
    human use for which a drug identification number has been assigned:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} drugs included in Schedule I, II, III, IV or V to
      the [Controlled Drugs and Substances Act](/eng/acts/C-38.8);

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prescription drugs;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} drugs that are listed in Schedule C or D to the
      Act; and

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} drugs that are permitted to be sold without a
      prescription but that are to be administered only under the
      supervision of a practitioner. ([drogue]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

[[shortage]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[shortage]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a drug, means a
    situation in which the manufacturer to whom a document was issued
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification
    number assigned for the drug is unable to meet the demand for the
    drug in Canada. ([pénurie]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- **[[C.01.014.9]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.9
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a shortage of a drug exists or is
  likely to occur, the manufacturer to whom a document was issued under
  subsection C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification number
  assigned for the drug shall post the following information in English
  and French on a website that is operated by a party for that purpose
  with whom Her Majesty in right of Canada has entered into a contract
  to make that information available to the public:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer's name and their telephone number,
    email address, website address, postal address or any other
    information that enables communication with them;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the drug identification number assigned for the
    drug;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the drug's brand name and proper name or, if it
    does not have a proper name, its common name;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the proper names of the drug's medicinal
    ingredients or, if they do not have proper names, their common
    names;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the drug's therapeutic classification according to
    the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification system (ATC),
    established by the World Health Organization Collaborating Centre
    for Drug Statistics Methodology --- namely the level 3 description
    of, and level 4 code for, the drug;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the drug's strength;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the drug's dosage form;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug contained in its package;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the drug's route of administration;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the date when the shortage began or is anticipated
    to begin;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the anticipated date when the manufacturer will be
    able to meet the demand for the drug, if they can anticipate that
    date; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the actual or anticipated reason for the shortage.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer shall post the information

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if they anticipate that a shortage will begin in
    more than six months, at least six months before the day on which
    they anticipate it to begin;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if they anticipate that a shortage will begin in
    six months or less, within five days after the day on which they
    anticipate it; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if they did not anticipate the shortage, within
    five days after the day on which they become aware of it.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If any of the information that was posted by the
  manufacturer changes, they shall update that information on the
  website within two days after the day on which they make or become
  aware of the change.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Within two days after the day on which the
  manufacturer is able to meet the demand for the drug, they shall post
  information on the website to that effect.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of a shortage
  of a drug that results from a decision by the manufacturer to
  discontinue its sale.

:::

- **[[C.01.014.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may request that the
  manufacturer to whom a document was issued under subsection
  C.01.014.2(1) that sets out the drug identification number assigned
  for a drug --- or any person who holds an establishment licence in
  respect of a drug --- provide the Minister with information that is in
  their control if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is a shortage or risk of shortage of the

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} measures that could be taken to prevent or
      alleviate a shortage of the drug; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer or licensee will not provide the
    information without a legal obligation to do so.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer or licensee shall provide the
  requested information electronically in a format specified by or
  acceptable to the Minister within the time limit specified by the
  Minister.

**[[C.01.014.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.014.13 .sectionLabel}** No
person who holds an establishment licence shall distribute a drug for
consumption or use outside Canada unless the licensee has reasonable
grounds to believe that the distribution will not cause or exacerbate a
shortage of the drug.

  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a person who holds an
  establishment licence distributes a drug for consumption or use
  outside Canada, the licensee shall immediately create a detailed
  record of the information that they relied on to determine that the
  distribution of the drug is not prohibited by section C.01.014.13.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The licensee shall retain the record for at least one
  year after the latest expiration date of the drug that they
  distributed.

#### [Tablet Disintegration Times]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575074 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.015]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.015
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall sell for human use a drug in the form of a tablet that is
  intended to be swallowed whole unless, when tested by the official
  method DO-25, Determination of the Disintegration Time of Tablets,
  dated July 5, 1989,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an uncoated tablet, the tablet
    disintegrates in not more than 45 minutes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a plain coated tablet, the tablet
    disintegrates in not more than 60 minutes; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the label of the drug indicates
    that the tablet carries an enteric coating or a coating designed to
    serve a purpose similar to that of an enteric coating, the tablet
    does not disintegrate when exposed for 60 minutes to simulated
    gastric fluid, but when it is subsequently exposed for a continuous
    period to simulated intestinal fluid, the tablet disintegrates in
    not more than 60 minutes.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a drug in
  the form of a tablet where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice of compliance in respect of the drug in
    the form of a tablet has been issued under section C.08.004 or
    C.08.004.01;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/98-423, s. 7\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a dissolution or disintegration test for the drug
    in the form of a tablet is prescribed in Division 6 of this Part;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the drug is labelled as complying with a standard
    contained in a publication referred to in Schedule B to the Act;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the drug has been demonstrated by an acceptable
    method to be available to the body; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} representations regarding the drug are made on its
    label, or in any advertisement, with respect to the site, rate or
    extent of release to the body of a medicinal ingredient of that
    drug, or the availability to the body of a medicinal ingredient of
    that drug.

#### [Serious Adverse Drug Reaction Reporting --- Manufacturers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575093 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2019-190, s. 1

\]
:::

**[[C.01.017]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.017 .sectionLabel}** The
manufacturer shall submit to the Minister a report of all information
relating to the following serious adverse drug reactions within 15 days
after receiving or becoming aware of the information, whichever occurs
first:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} any serious adverse drug reaction that has occurred
  in Canada with respect to the drug; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any serious unexpected adverse drug reaction that has
  occurred outside Canada with respect to the drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/95-521, s. 2
- SOR/2011-31, s. 1
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.017-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.017"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Annual Summary Report and Case Reports]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575099 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.018]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.018
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer shall prepare an
  annual summary report of all information relating to adverse drug
  reactions and serious adverse drug reactions to the drug that it
  received or became aware of during the previous 12 months.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The annual summary report shall contain a concise,
  critical analysis of the adverse drug reactions and serious adverse
  drug reactions to the drug.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In preparing the annual summary report, the
  manufacturer shall determine, on the basis of the analysis referred to
  in subsection (2), whether there has been a significant change in what
  is known about the risks and benefits of the drug during the period
  covered by the report and shall include its conclusions in this regard
  in the summary report.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If, in preparing the annual summary report, the
  manufacturer concludes that there has been a significant change, it
  shall notify the Minister without delay, in writing, unless this has
  already been done.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, for the purposes of assessing the
  safety and effectiveness of the drug, request in writing that the
  manufacturer submit to the Minister one or both of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the annual summary reports;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the case reports relating to the adverse drug
    reactions and serious adverse drug reactions to the drug that are
    known to the manufacturer.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, after giving the manufacturer an
  opportunity to be heard, specify a period for the submission of the
  annual summary reports or case reports, or both, that is reasonable in
  the circumstances, and the manufacturer shall submit the reports
  within that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-31, s. 1
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.018-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.018"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.018.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.018.1 .sectionLabel}** Section
C.01.018 does not apply in respect of a veterinary health product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2017-76, s. 4
:::

#### [Issue-Related Summary Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575114 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.019]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.019
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, for the purposes
  of assessing the safety and effectiveness of the drug, request in
  writing that the manufacturer submit to the Minister an issue-related
  summary report.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The report shall contain a concise, critical analysis
  of the adverse drug reactions and serious adverse drug reactions to
  the drug, as well as case reports of all or specified adverse drug
  reactions and serious adverse drug reactions to the drug that are
  known to the manufacturer in respect of the issue that the Minister
  directs the manufacturer to analyze in the report.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, after giving the manufacturer an
  opportunity to be heard, specify a period for the submission of the
  report that is reasonable in the circumstances. The Minister may only
  specify a period that is less than 30 days if the Minister needs the
  information in the report to determine whether the drug poses a
  serious and imminent risk to human health.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer shall submit the report within the
  specified period.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-31, s. 1
- SOR/2017-18, s. 14
:::

- **[[C.01.020]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.020
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer shall maintain
  records of the reports and case reports referred to in sections
  C.01.017 to C.01.019.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer shall retain the records for 25

#### [Provision of Information Under Section 21.8 of Act]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1214780 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.020.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.020.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 21.8 of
  the Act, hospitals are the prescribed health care institutions that
  shall provide information that is in their control to the Minister
  about a serious adverse drug reaction.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following prescribed information about a serious
  adverse drug reaction that is in a hospital's control shall be
  provided to the Minister in writing within 30 days after the day on
  which the serious adverse drug reaction is first documented within the
  hospital:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the hospital and the contact
    information of a representative of that hospital;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the drug's brand name, proper name or common name;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug imported under subsection
    C.10.001(2) or section C.10.006, the identifying code or number of
    the drug, if any, assigned in the country in which the drug was
    authorized for sale;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug whose sale has been
    authorized under subsection C.11.003(1), its identifying name, code,
    number or mark;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the drug identification number assigned for the
    drug, if applicable;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the patient's age and sex;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a description of the serious adverse drug reaction;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the serious adverse drug reaction
    was first documented;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the patient first used the drug
    and, if applicable, the date on which the patient stopped using the
    drug;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the serious adverse drug reaction
    first occurred and, if applicable, the date on which the patient's
    health was restored to its state prior to the reaction;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} any medical condition of the patient that directly
    relates to the serious adverse drug reaction;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} any concomitant therapeutic products used by the
    patient; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the effect of the serious adverse drug reaction on
    the patient's health.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A hospital is exempt from section 21.8 of the Act in
  respect of the reporting of information referred to in subsection (2)
  if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the hospital does not have in its control all of
    the information referred to in paragraphs (2)(b), (c), (e) and (f)
    in respect of the serious adverse drug reaction; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the serious adverse drug reaction relates only to
    any of the following drugs:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a vaccine that was administered under a routine
      immunization program of a province,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a drug that is authorized for sale under
      Division 5 of this Part, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a drug that was sold under subsection
      C.08.011(1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[hospital]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  means a facility

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that is licensed, approved or designated as a
    hospital by a province in accordance with the laws of the province
    to provide care or treatment to persons suffering from any form of
    disease or illness; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is operated by the Government of Canada and
    that provides health services to in-patients.

#### [Limits of Drug Dosage]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575131 .Subheading}

**[[C.01.021]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.021 .sectionLabel}** Except as
provided in these Regulations, no person shall sell a drug for human use
listed in the following table unless both the inner and the outer labels
other than the inner label of a single dose container carry a statement
of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the quantitative content of the drug,

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the recommended single and daily adult dose
  designated as such, except for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} preparations solely for external use, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} preparations solely for children's use; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} adequate directions for use when the drug is
  recommended for children which shall be either

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the statement "CHILDREN: As directed by the
    physician", or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a suitable reduced maximum single and daily dose
    which shall not exceed the following:

    Where drugs having similar physiological actions occur in
    combination, the dosage of each shall be proportionately reduced.

    Accurate dosagesmay be expressed in either metric units or imperial
    units. If the dosage is expressed in both systems, then an
    approximation may be used for one expression, but such approximation
    must precede or follow the accurate statement by which the product
    will be judged and must be in brackets.

**[[C.01.022]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.022
.sectionLabel}** Notwithstanding paragraph C.01.021(b), the recommended
single and daily dosage of a drug

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} intended to be burned and the smoke inhaled may be
  increased to 10 times the oral dose, and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} intended for use as suppositories may be increased to
  33 1/3 per cent in excess of the oral dose.

<!-- -->

- **[[C.01.024]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.024
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections C.01.021 and C.01.022 do
  not apply to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drug sold to a drug manufacturer; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a drug sold on prescription.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph C.01.021(c) does not apply to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} acetaminophen;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} acetylsalicylic acid;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} magnesium salicylate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} sodium salicylate; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} choline salicylate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a drug mentioned in any of paragraphs (2)(a)
  to (d) is recommended for children, no person shall sell the drug for
  human use unless both the inner and the outer labels carry a statement
  that it is recommended

    or

    amounts set out in the following table and that single doses not be

**[[C.01.025]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.025 .sectionLabel}** Both the
inner and the outer labels of a drug that carry a recommended single or
daily dosage or a statement of concentration in excess of the limits
provided by section C.01.021 shall carry a caution that the product is
to be used only on the advice of a physician.

**[[C.01.026]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.026 .sectionLabel}** The
provisions of section C.01.025 do not apply to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drug sold on prescription, or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the inner label of a single-dose container.

<!-- -->

- **[[C.01.027]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.027
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a person advertises to the
  general public a drug for human use, the person shall not make any
  representation other than with respect to the brand name, proper name,
  common name, price and quantity of the drug if it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} contains a drug set out in the table to section
    C.01.021; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} carries on its label

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a statement of the recommended single or daily
      adult dosage that results in a single or daily adult dosage of the
      drug referred to in paragraph (a) in excess of the maximum dosage
      set out in the table to section C.01.021 for that drug, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a statement that shows a concentration of the
      drug referred to in paragraph (a) in excess of the maximum limit
      set out in the table to section C.01.021 for that drug.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to products containing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} acetaminophen;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} acetylsalicylic acid;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} choline salicylate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} magnesium salicylate; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} sodium salicylate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/94-409, s. 1\]]{.Repealed}

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a person advertises to the general public a
  drug for human use that contains acetylsalicylic acid, the person
  shall not make any representation with respect to its administration
  to or use by children or teenagers.

#### [Cautionary Statements and Child Resistant Packages]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575210 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.028]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.028
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the inner
  and outer labels of a drug that contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} acetylsalicylic acid or any of its salts or
    derivatives, salicylic acid or a salt thereof, or salicylamide,
    where the drug is recommended for children, shall carry a cautionary
    statement to the effect that the drug should not be administered to
    a child under two years of age except on the advice of a physician;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} boric acid or sodium borate as a medicinal
    ingredient shall carry a cautionary statement to the effect that the
    drug should not be administered to a child under three years of age;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} hyoscine (scopolamine) or a salt thereof shall
    carry a cautionary statement to the effect that the drug should not
    be used by persons suffering from glaucoma or where it causes
    blurring of the vision or pressure pain within the eye;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} phenacetin, either singly or in combination with
    other drugs, shall carry the following cautionary statement:

    > ::: QuotedText
    > "CAUTION: May be injurious if taken in large doses or for a long
    > time. Do not exceed the recommended dose without consulting a
    > physician."; or
    > :::

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} acetylsalicylic acid for internal use shall carry a
    cautionary statement to the effect that the drug should not be
    administered to or used by children or teenagers who have chicken
    pox or manifest flu symptoms before a physician or pharmacist is
    consulted about Reye's syndrome, which statement shall also refer to
    the fact that Reye's syndrome is a rare and serious illness.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to a drug that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} intended for parenteral use only;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} dispensed pursuant to a prescription; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a prescription drug or a drug that is required to
    be sold under a prescription by Part G, the [Benzodiazepines and
    Other Targeted Substances
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-217) or the [Narcotic Control
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1041).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/86-93, s. 2
- SOR/88-323, s. 2(F)
- SOR/93-411, s. 2
- SOR/2013-122, s. 7
:::

- **[[C.01.029]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.029
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections C.01.031.2(1)
  and (2), the inner and outer labels of a drug

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that contains

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} salicylic acid, a salt thereof or salicylamide,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} acetylsalicylic acid, or any of its salts or
      derivatives,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} acetaminophen, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} more than five per cent alkyl salicylates,

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} that contains nicotine or any of its salts and is
    a [[vaping product]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section 2
    of the [Tobacco and Vaping Products Act](/eng/acts/T-11.5) but that
    is not referred to in paragraph 2(b) or (c) or section 3 of the
    [Regulations Excluding Certain Vaping Products Regulated Under the
    Food and Drugs Act from the Application of the Tobacco and Vaping
    Products Act](/eng/regulations/SOR-2018-133), or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is in a package that contains

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} more than the equivalent of 250 mg of elemental
      iron, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} more than the equivalent of 120 mg of fluoride
      ion, unless the drug is intended solely for use in dentists'
      offices,

  shall carry a cautionary statement to the effect that the drug should
  be kept out of the reach of children.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections C.01.031.2(1) and (2), the
  inner label and outer label of a drug that is in a package shall carry
  a cautionary statement, to the effect that there is enough drug in the
  package to seriously harm a child, if the package contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} more than 1.5 g of salicylic acid or the equivalent
    quantity of any of its salts or salicylamide,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} more than 2 g of acetylsalicylic acid or the
    equivalent quantity of any of its salts or derivatives,

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} more than 3.2 g of acetaminophen,

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} more than the equivalent of 250 mg of elemental
    iron,

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} more than the equivalent of 120 mg of fluoride ion,
    unless the drug is intended solely for use in dentists' offices, or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the drug is a [[vaping
    product]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in section 2 of the
    [Tobacco and Vaping Products Act](/eng/acts/T-11.5) but is not
    referred to in paragraph 2(b) or (c) or section 3 of the
    [Regulations Excluding Certain Vaping Products Regulated Under the
    Food and Drugs Act from the Application of the Tobacco and Vaping
    Products Act](/eng/regulations/SOR-2018-133), 0.1 mg/ml or more of
    nicotine or the equivalent quantity of any of its salts.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The cautionary statements required under
  subsections (1) and (2) shall be preceded by a prominently displayed
  symbol that is octagonal in shape, conspicuous in colour and on a
  background of a contrasting colour.

- **[[C.01.031]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.031
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section C.01.031.2,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no person shall sell a drug described in subsection
    C.01.029(1) unless

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where the drug is recommended solely for
      children, it is packaged in a child resistant package,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the drug is not recommended solely for
      children, other than a drug referred to in subparagraph (iii), at
      least one of the sizes of packages available for sale is packaged
      in a child resistant package, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the drug is a vaping product referred to
      in paragraph C.01.029(1)(a.1), it is packaged in a child resistant
      package; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a drug described in subsection C.01.029(1) is
    packaged in a package that is not a child resistant package, the
    outer label shall carry a statement that the drug is available in a
    child resistant package.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection C.01.031.2(2) and paragraph
  C.01.031.2(3)(a) do not apply to a drug referred to in paragraph
  C.01.029(1)(a.1).

- **[[C.01.031.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.031.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections C.01.029 to C.01.031 do not
  apply to a drug that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a prescription drug or a drug that is required to
    be sold under a prescription by Part G, the [Benzodiazepines and
    Other Targeted Substances
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-217) or the [Narcotic Control
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1041);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} intended for parenteral use only;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in effervescent or powder form;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in suppository form;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} intended for topical use, unless it is a liquid
    preparation containing more than five per cent alkyl salicylates;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} packaged in a non-reclosable package containing not
    more than two adult standard dosage units per package; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in toothpaste form.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Sections C.01.029 to C.01.031 do not apply to a drug
  that is repackaged by a pharmacist or practitioner at the time of
  sale.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Section C.01.031 does not apply to a drug that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sold only in containers that have roll-on or spray
    applicators or permanently installed wick applicators;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sold for exclusive use in animals other than
    household pets; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} intended solely for use in dentists' offices, or
    packaged for hospital use only.

**[[C.01.032]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.032 .sectionLabel}** No person
shall sell a corticosteroid drug for ophthalmic use unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the outer label or the package insert carries, as
  part of the directions for use, the following statements:

  > ::: QuotedText
  > *"Contraindications*
  >
  > Viral diseases of the cornea and conjunctiva;
  >
  > Tuberculosis of the eye;
  >
  > Fungal diseases of the eye;
  >
  > Acute purulent untreated infections of the eye, which, like other
  > diseases caused by micro-organisms, may be masked or enhanced by the
  > presence of the steroid.
  >
  > *Side Effects*
  >
  > Extended ophthalmic use of corticosteroid drugs may cause increased
  > intraocular pressure in certain individuals and in those diseases
  > causing thinning of the cornea, perforation has been known to
  > occur.";
  > :::

  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the inner label carries the statements required by
  paragraph (a) or instructions to see the outer label or package insert
  for information about contraindications and side effects.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-69, s. 18(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.032-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.032"){.PITLink}
:::

C.01.032 does not apply to a corticosteroid drug that is sold by a
pharmacist under a prescription.

**[[C.01.034]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.034 .sectionLabel}** No person
shall disseminate to a practitioner promotional literature about
corticosteroid drugs for ophthalmic use unless the statements required
by paragraph C.01.032(a) are included in that literature.

**[[C.01.035]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.035 .sectionLabel}** Sections
C.01.032 and C.01.034 do not apply to a drug sold solely for veterinary
use.

#### [Miscellaneous]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575285 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.036]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.036
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No manufacturer or importer shall
  sell

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drug that contains phenacetin in combination with
    any salt or derivative of salicylic acid;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a drug for human use that contains

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} oxyphenisatin,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} oxyphenisatin acetate, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} phenisatin; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a drug for human use that contains mercury or a
    salt or derivative thereof, unless the drug is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a drug described in Schedule C or D to the Act,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one of the following drugs, namely,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an ophthalmic drug or other drug to be used in
        the area of the eye,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a drug for nasal administration,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a drug for otic administration, or

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} a drug for parenteral administration that is
        packaged in a multi-dose container,

    in which the mercury or the salt or derivative thereof is present as
    a preservative and the manufacturer or importer has submitted
    evidence to the Minister demonstrating that the only satisfactory
    way to maintain the sterility or stability of the drug is to use
    that preservative.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of clause (1)(c)(ii)(A), [[area of
  the eye]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the area bounded by the
  supraorbital and infraorbital ridges and includes the eyebrows, the
  skin underlying the eyebrows, the eyelids, the eyelashes, the
  conjunctival sac of the eye, the eyeball and the soft tissue that lies
  below the eye and within the infraorbital ridge.

  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall sell to the general

    units.

**[[C.01.038]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.038 .sectionLabel}** A drug for
human use is adulterated if it contains

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Strychnine or any of its salts;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} extracts or tinctures of

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} [Strychnos nux vomica]{.otherLang lang="la"},

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} [Strychnos Ignatii]{.otherLang lang="la"}, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a [Strychnos]{.otherLang lang="la"} species
    containing strychnine, other than those species mentioned in
    subparagraphs (i) and (ii);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} Methapyrilene or any of its salts;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} Echimidine or any of its salts; or

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} any of the following plant species or extracts or
  tinctures thereof:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} [Symphytum asperum]{.otherLang lang="la"},

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} [Symphytum x uplandicum]{.otherLang lang="la"}, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any other plant species containing echimidine.

#### [Colouring Agents]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575341 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.040.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.040.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No manufacturer shall use a
  colouring agent in a drug other than a colouring agent listed in
  subsections (3) and (4).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall import for sale a drug that contains
  a colouring agent other than a colouring agent listed in
  subsections (3) and (4).

- [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in subsections (3)
  to (4.1):

  [[C.I. (indication of the number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[C.I. (indication of the number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      designation used to identify a colouring agent in the Colour Index
      published by The Society of Dyers and Colourists, as amended from
      time to time; ([C.I. (indication du numéro)]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[D & C (indication of the colour and the number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[D & C (indication of the colour and the
      number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the designation used to
      identify, in accordance with the Code of Federal Regulations of
      the United States, a colouring agent that can be used in the
      United States in drugs and cosmetics; ([D&C (indication de la
      couleur et du numéro)]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[FD & C (indication of the colour and the number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      number)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the designation used to
      identify, in accordance with the Code of Federal Regulations of
      the United States, a colouring agent that can be used in the
      United States in food, drugs and cosmetics. ([FD&C (indication de
      la couleur et du numéro)]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), no manufacturer shall use a
  preparation made by extending any of the following substances on a
  substratum of mica in a drug unless the requirements in subsection
  (4.3) are met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} titanium dioxide (C.I. No. 77891);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} iron oxides (C.I. Nos. 77489, 77491, 77492, 77499);
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a mixed oxide made from substances referred to in
    both paragraphs (a) and (b).

- [(4.2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), no person shall import for
  sale a drug that contains a preparation made by extending any of the
  substances referred to in paragraphs (4.1)(a) to (c) on a substratum
  of mica unless the requirements in subsection (4.3) are met.

- [(4.3)]{.lawlabel} The requirements referred to in subsections (4.1)
  and (4.2) are the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the drug shall be in a solid dosage form intended
    for oral administration or in a liquid dosage form intended for oral
    administration or it shall be a drug intended for external use;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the drug is in a solid dosage
    form intended for oral administration, the drug shall not contain
    more than 3% of the preparation;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the preparation was made using
    iron oxides, the preparation shall not contain more than 55% iron
    oxides.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1), (2), (4.1) and (4.2) do not apply in
  respect of a drug that is represented as being solely for use in the
  disinfection, for disease prevention, of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} medical devices;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} health care facilities; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} premises in which food is manufactured, prepared or
    kept.

#### [Prescription Drugs]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575463 .Subheading}

**[[C.01.040.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.040.3 .sectionLabel}** In
deciding whether to amend the Prescription Drug List in respect of a
drug, including by adding the drug to it or removing the drug from it,
the Minister shall consider whether any of the following criteria apply
with respect to the drug:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} supervision by a practitioner is necessary

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or
    prevention of a disease, disorder or abnormal physical state, or its
    symptoms, in respect of which the drug is recommended for use, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to monitor a disease, disorder or abnormal
    physical state, or its symptoms, in respect of which the drug is
    recommended for use, or to monitor the use of the drug;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the level of uncertainty respecting the drug, its use
  or its effects justifies supervision by a practitioner; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} use of the drug can cause harm to human or animal
  health or a risk to public health and the harm or the risk can be
  mitigated by a practitioner's supervision.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2013-122, s. 10
- SOR/2017-18, s. 21(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.040.3-20131219.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.040.3"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.040.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.040.4 .sectionLabel}** The
Minister shall consult the general public on any proposal by the
Minister to remove a drug from the Prescription Drug List.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2013-122, s. 10
:::

**[[C.01.040.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.040.5 .sectionLabel}** Sections
C.01.040.3 and C.01.040.4 apply, with any modifications that the
circumstances require, in respect of classes of drugs.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2013-122, s. 10
:::

- **[[C.01.041]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.041
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall sell a prescription
  drug unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they are entitled under the laws of a province to
    dispense a prescription drug and they sell it in that province under
    a verbal or written prescription that they received; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} they sell it under section C.01.043.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a verbal prescription, the person
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or a pharmacy technician shall create
  a written record of the prescription that includes the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the prescription was received
    and, if applicable, the number of the prescription;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person to whom the
    prescription was issued;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the proper name, common name or brand name of the
    drug and its quantity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and the name of the practitioner
    who issued the prescription; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the directions for use provided with the
    prescription, whether or not the practitioner authorized it to be
    refilled and, if refills are authorized, the number of authorized
    refills.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person referred to in paragraph (1)(a) shall
  retain the written prescription referred to in subsection (1) or the
  record referred to in subsection (2) for at least two years after the
  day on which the prescription is filled.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 2
- SOR/80-543, s. 3
- SOR/93-202, s. 6
- SOR/93-407, s. 2
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

Version](section-C.01.041-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.041"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.041.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.041.1 .sectionLabel}** Subject
to paragraph C.01.041.3(2)(b), a pharmacist or pharmacy technician may
transfer to another pharmacist or pharmacy technician a prescription for
a prescription drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 3
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.041.1-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.041.1"){.PITLink}
:::

- **[[C.01.041.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.041.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before a pharmacist sells a drug
  under a prescription that was transferred under section C.01.041.1,
  the pharmacist or a pharmacy technician shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} create a written record of the name and address of
    the pharmacist or pharmacy technician who transferred the
    prescription and, if applicable, the number of authorized refills
    remaining and the date of the last refill; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} obtain a copy of the written prescription or of the
    written record that was created under subsection C.01.041(2), as the
    case may be, or, in the case of a verbal transfer, create a written
    record that includes the information referred to in that subsection.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pharmacist shall retain the documents referred to
  in subsection (1) for at least two years after the day on which the
  prescription was filled.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 3
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.041.2-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.041.2"){.PITLink}
:::

- **[[C.01.041.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.041.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pharmacist or a pharmacy
  technician who transfers a prescription under section C.01.041.1 shall
  indicate the date of transfer on the original of the written
  prescription or of the written record created under subsection
  C.01.041(2) or in a record kept under the name of the patient in
  question, as the case may be.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the pharmacist or pharmacy technician has
  transferred the prescription,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pharmacist shall not make any additional sales
    under the prescription; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pharmacist or pharmacy technician shall not
    transfer the prescription to another pharmacist or pharmacy
    technician.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 3
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

**[[C.01.042]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.042 .sectionLabel}** A person
referred to in paragraph C.01.041(1)(a) shall not refill a prescription
for a prescription drug unless authorized by the practitioner and, in
the case of such an authorization, they shall not refill a prescription
more than the number of times specified by the practitioner.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 4
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.042-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.042"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.042.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.042.1 .sectionLabel}** A person
referred to in paragraph C.01.041(1)(a) shall indicate on the original
of or on the copy of the written prescription or the written record
created under subsection C.01.041(2) or in a record kept under the name
of the patient in question, as the case may be,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the prescription was filled;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date of each refill, if applicable;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of drug sold when the prescription was
  filled and, if applicable, for each refill; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person who sold the drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

- **[[C.01.043]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.043
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person may sell a prescription
  drug to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drug manufacturer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a practitioner;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a wholesale druggist;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a pharmacist; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the Government of Canada or the government of a
    province, for the use of a department or agency of that government,
    on receipt of a written order signed by the minister responsible for
    the department or by the person in charge of the agency, or by their
    duly authorized representative.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person sells a prescription drug under paragraph
  (1)(e), they shall retain the written order for the drug for a period
  of at least two years after the day on which the drug is sold.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-C.01.043-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.043"){.PITLink}

**[[C.01.044]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.044 .sectionLabel}** If a person
advertises a prescription drug to the general public, the person shall
not make any representation other than with respect to the brand name,
the proper name, the common name and the price and quantity of the drug.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/78-424, s. 5
- SOR/93-202, s. 7
- SOR/93-407, s. 3
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

::: PITLink

Version](section-C.01.044-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section C.01.044"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[C.01.045]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.045 .sectionLabel}** No person,
other than one of the following, shall import a prescription drug:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a practitioner;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a drug manufacturer;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a wholesale druggist;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a pharmacist; or

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a resident of a foreign country while a visitor in
  Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/93-407, s. 4
- SOR/2013-122, s. 11
:::

#### [Distribution of Drugs as Samples]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1254042 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2020-74, s. 2

\]
:::

- **[[C.01.048]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.048
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a practitioner or pharmacist has
  signed an order specifying the proper name or common name, the brand
  name and the quantity of a drug, other than the following, the person
  who receives the order may distribute or cause to be distributed the
  drug, in dosage form, as a sample to that practitioner or pharmacist
  if the drug meets the requirements of these Regulations:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a [[narcotic]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as defined in
    the [Narcotic Control
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1041);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a [[controlled drug]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as
    defined in section G.01.001; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2020-74, s. 3\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a [[prescription drug]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} as
    defined in subsection 1(2) of the [Cannabis
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2018-144).

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A person may distribute or cause to be distributed
  a prescription drug as a sample under subsection (1) only to a
  practitioner or pharmacist who is entitled, under the laws of the
  province in which they are practising, to prescribe or dispense that
  drug, as the case may be.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An order referred to in subsection (1) may provide
  that the order be repeated at specified intervals during any period
  not exceeding six months.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may distribute or
  cause to be distributed a drug, in dosage form, as a sample to a
  practitioner or pharmacist without a signed order if that drug is not
  a prescription drug and is part of a class of drugs that is set out in
  column 1 of List D, and if all of the following conditions are met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the drug contains, as its only medicinal
    ingredients, one or more of those set out in column 2, each of which
    corresponds to that class, in the corresponding quantity set out in
    column 3, and the drug is consistent with the descriptive
    information set out in columns 4 to 6;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the expiration date of the drug falls on a day that
    is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at least 30 days after the day on which it is
      distributed, if the expiration date consists of a day, month and
      year, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in a month that follows the month in which it is
      distributed, if the expiration date consists only of a month and
      year;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the drug meets the requirements of these
    Regulations.

::: HistoricalNote

- SOR/97-228, s. 2
- SOR/2018-144, s. 366

**[[C.01.049]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.049 .sectionLabel}** A person who,
under subsection C.01.048(1), receives an order for and distributes or
causes to be distributed a drug as a sample shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain records showing

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and description of each person to
    whom the drug is distributed,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the brand name, quantity and form of the drug
    distributed, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the date upon which each such distribution was
    made; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep those records and all orders received for drugs
  in accordance with section C.01.048 for a period of not less than two
  years from the date upon which the distribution referred to in the
  records was made.

::: HistoricalNote

**[[C.01.049.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.049.1 .sectionLabel}** A person
may distribute or cause to be distributed a drug, in dosage form, as a
sample to any consumer that is 18 years of age or older if that drug is
not a prescription drug and is part of a class of drugs that is set out
in column 1 of List D, and if all of the following conditions are met:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the drug contains, as its only medicinal ingredients,
  one or more of those set out in column 2, each of which corresponds to
  that class, in the corresponding quantity set out in column 3, and the
  drug is consistent with the descriptive information set out in columns
  4 to 6;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the expiration date of the drug falls on a day that
  is

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at least 30 days after the day on which it is
    distributed, if the expiration date consists of a day, month and
    year, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in a month that follows the month in which it is
    distributed, if the expiration date consists only of a month and
    year;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the drug meets the requirements of these Regulations.

#### [Information --- Serious Risk of Injury to Human Health]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575559 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.050]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.050
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies to a holder of
  one or more of the following therapeutic product authorizations:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drug identification number that has been assigned
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a notice of compliance that has been issued under
    section C.08.004 or C.08.004.01.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a therapeutic product authorization in
  respect of a drug that is part of a class of drugs set out in
  subsection (4) shall provide the Minister with information in respect
  of any serious risk of injury to human health that the holder receives
  or becomes aware of and that is relevant to the safety of the drug,
  regarding

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} risks that have been communicated by any foreign
    regulatory authority that is set out in Part A of the List of
    Foreign Regulatory Authorities for the Purposes of Section C.01.050
    of the Food and Drug Regulations, published by the Government of
    Canada on its website, as amended from time to time, or by any
    person who is authorized to manufacture or sell a drug within the
    jurisdiction of such an authority, and the manner of the
    communication;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} changes that have been made to the labelling of any
    drug and that have been communicated to or requested by any foreign
    regulatory authority that is set out in Part B of the list referred
    to in paragraph (a); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} recalls, reassessments and suspensions or
    revocations of authorizations, including licences, in respect of any
    drug, that have taken place within the jurisdiction of any foreign
    regulatory authority that is set out in Part C of the list referred
    to in paragraph (a).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The information shall be provided to the Minister
  within 72 hours after the holder receives or becomes aware of it,
  whichever occurs first.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The classes of drugs are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prescription drugs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} drugs that are required to be sold under a
    prescription by Part G, the [Benzodiazepines and Other Targeted
    Substances Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2000-217) or the
    [Narcotic Control Regulations](/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._1041);
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} drugs that are permitted to be sold without a
    prescription but that are to be administered only under the
    supervision of a practitioner.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a holder of a therapeutic
  product authorization who provided information in accordance with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraph (2)(a) is not required to provide the
    same information again under that paragraph in the case where the
    holder receives or becomes aware of that information in respect of a
    foreign regulatory authority or person referred to in that
    paragraph; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraph (2)(b) or (c) is not required to provide
    the same information again under that paragraph in the case where
    the holder receives or becomes aware of that information in respect
    of a foreign regulatory authority referred to in that paragraph.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[foreign regulatory
  authority]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a government agency or other
  entity outside Canada that has a legal right to control the
  manufacturing, use or sale of drugs within its jurisdiction and that
  may take enforcement action to ensure that drugs marketed within its
  jurisdiction comply with the applicable legal requirements.

#### [Recall Reporting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575579 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.051]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.051
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a manufacturer who sells a drug
  in dosage form or an active ingredient or a person who imports into
  and sells a drug in dosage form or an active ingredient in Canada
  decides to recall any of those drugs without being ordered to do so by
  the Minister, the manufacturer or importer shall, within 24 hours
  after making the decision, provide the Minister with the following
  information in writing:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the drug's proper name or the common name, if there
    is no proper name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an indication as to whether the drug is a drug in
    dosage form or an active ingredient;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a drug in dosage form,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the brand name,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the drug identification number assigned under
      subsection C.01.014.2(1),

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the dosage form,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the strength,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the names of the persons in Canada, other than
      consumers that purchased the drug at the retail level, to whom the
      drug was sold by the manufacturer or importer and the quantity
      sold to each of the named persons, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} an assessment of the effect that the recall may
      have on the manufacturer's or importer's ability to meet demand
      for the drug in Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the lot numbers of the drug;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dates of fabrication of the drug;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the expiration dates of the drug;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that was fabricated in
    Canada;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that was imported;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that the manufacturer or
    importer sold to persons in Canada and the period during which it
    was sold;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that the manufacturer or
    importer exported, as well as the quantity exported, by country;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug in Canada that is in the
    possession or control of the manufacturer or importer;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} an assessment of the risk of injury to human health
    posed by the drug, including because of a failure of its
    effectiveness;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} the names and civic addresses of the manufacturer
    and fabricator of the drug and of any importers of the drug;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the individual
    who is responsible for the recall;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} the expected dates for the start and completion of
    the recall; and

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} the reasons for the recall and the date on which
    and manner in which the situation that prompted the recall was
    discovered.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer or importer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before starting the recall, provide the Minister
    with a copy of any communications that the manufacturer or importer
    intends to use in connection with the start of the recall; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} after starting the recall, provide the Minister, on
    request and within the time specified by the Minister, with a copy
    of any additional communications that the manufacturer or importer
    uses, or intends to use, in connection with the recall.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer or importer shall, within 72 hours
  after making the decision to recall the drug, provide the Minister
  with the following information in writing:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the strategy for conducting the recall, including
    the time and manner in which the Minister will be informed of the
    progress of the recall; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the measures that are intended to
    be taken to prevent a recurrence of the situation that prompted the
    recall.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The manufacturer or importer shall, within 30 days
  after completing the recall, provide the Minister with the following
  information in writing:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the results of the recall; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the measures that have been or
    will be taken to prevent a recurrence of the situation that prompted
    the recall.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} In this section and in section C.01.051.1, [[active
  ingredient]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} and
  [[fabricate]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} have the same meaning as in
  subsection C.01A.001(1).

- **[[C.01.051.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.051.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who is ordered by the
  Minister under section 21.3 of the Act to recall a drug in dosage
  form, or an active ingredient, shall provide the Minister with the
  following information in the time and manner specified by the
  Minister:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that has been sold by the
    person at the retail level to consumers in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the person has sold the drug to persons in
    Canada other than consumers referred to in paragraph (a),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the names of those persons and the quantity that
      has been sold to each of them, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the period during which the drug was sold to
      those persons;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug that the person has
    exported from Canada, as well as the quantity exported by country;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the quantity of the drug in Canada that is in the
    possession or control of the person;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the name, title and contact information of an
    individual from whom the Minister may obtain additional information
    concerning the recall;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the strategy for conducting the recall;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} any other information that the Minister has
    reasonable grounds to believe is necessary to mitigate the risk of
    injury to human health; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} if the person is in a position to prevent a
    recurrence of the situation that prompted the recall, a description
    of the measures that they intend to take to prevent a recurrence.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person shall notify the Minister without delay of
  any change to the information referred to in paragraph (1)(e).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before starting the recall, provide the Minister
    with a copy of any communications that the person intends to use in
    connection with the start of the recall; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} after starting the recall, provide the Minister
    with, on request and within the time specified by the Minister, a
    copy of any additional communications that the person uses, or
    intends to use, in connection with the recall.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The person shall notify the Minister in writing,
  within 24 hours, of the start and completion of the recall.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The person shall, within 30 days after completing the
  recall, provide the Minister with the following information in
  writing:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the results of the recall; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the person is in a position to prevent a
    recurrence of the situation that prompted the recall, a description
    of the measures that they have taken or will take to prevent a
    recurrence.

#### [Assessments Ordered Under Section 21.31 of the Act]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575590 .Subheading}

- **[[C.01.052]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.052
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister's power to make an
  order under section 21.31 of the Act in respect of a drug is subject
  to the following conditions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person to whom the order is made shall be the
    holder of one or more of the following therapeutic product
    authorizations in respect of the drug:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a drug identification number that has been
      assigned under subsection C.01.014.2(1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an establishment licence that has been issued
      under subsection C.01A.008(1), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a notice of compliance that has been issued
      under section C.08.004 or C.08.004.01; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Minister shall have reasonable grounds to
    believe that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic product
      authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(i) or (iii), the
      benefits or risks of injury to health associated with the drug are
      significantly different than they were when the authorization was
      issued,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic product
      authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii) who is an
      importer, the manner in which one or more of the following
      activities is conducted may present a risk of injury to health
      associated with the drug:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} [[importation]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as
        defined in subsection C.01A.001(1), of the drug,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} [[fabrication]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} or
        [[packaging/labelling]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in
        subsection C.01A.001(1), of the drug outside Canada, or

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} testing of the drug outside Canada, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic
      product authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii) who is
      not an importer, the manner in which an activity that is
      authorized under the authorization is conducted may present a risk
      of injury to health associated with the drug.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, after examining the results of an
  assessment that was ordered under section 21.31 of the Act in respect
  of a drug,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide the holder of the therapeutic product
    authorization with the results of the examination; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that a summary of the results of the
    examination, together with a description of any steps that the
    Minister has taken or may take as a consequence of the examination,
    is published on the Government of Canada website.

#### [Activities Ordered Under Section 21.32 of the Act]{.HTitleText3} {#h-575610 .Subheading}

**[[C.01.053]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-C.01.053 .sectionLabel}** The
Minister's power to make an order under section 21.32 of the Act in
respect of a drug is subject to the following conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person to whom the order is made shall be the
  holder of one or more of the following therapeutic product
  authorizations in respect of the drug:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a drug identification number that has been assigned
    under subsection C.01.014.2(1),

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an establishment licence that has been issued
    under subsection C.01A.008(1), and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a notice of compliance that has been issued under
    section C.08.004 or C.08.004.01;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Minister shall have reasonable grounds to believe
  that

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic product
    authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(i) or (iii), there are
    significant uncertainties relating to the benefits or harms
    associated with the drug,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic product
    authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii) who is an
    importer, the manner in which one or more of the following
    activities is conducted has introduced significant uncertainties
    relating to the benefits or harms associated with the drug:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} [[importation]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined
      in subsection C.01A.001(1), of the drug,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} [[fabrication]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} or
      [[packaging/labelling]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in
      subsection C.01A.001(1), of the drug outside Canada, or

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} testing of the drug outside Canada,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a holder of a therapeutic product
    authorization referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii) who is not an
    importer, the manner in which an activity that is authorized under
    the authorization is conducted has introduced significant
    uncertainties relating to the benefits or harms associated with the
    drug,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the therapeutic product
    authorization is unable to provide the Minister with information
    that is sufficient to manage those uncertainties, and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the applicable requirements of these Regulations,
    together with any terms and conditions that have been imposed on the
    authorization, do not allow for sufficient information to be
    obtained to manage those uncertainties; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Minister shall take into account the following
  matters:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} whether the activities that the holder of the
    therapeutic product authorization will be ordered to undertake are
    feasible, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} whether there are less burdensome ways of
    obtaining additional information about the drug's effects on health
    or safety.
